reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). The majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carried ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-01); ticket response times remain within SLA (E-04) and no tariff change occurred (E-02). The best-supported mechanism (H-RULE-CHANGE) is that a billing import validation-rule change around August is producing incorrect calculated bills even on correctly-read accounts, driving most of the surge, with a smaller secondary contribution from estimate-substitution tied to the route-completion gap (E-03).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). The best-supported mechanism (H-RULE-CHANGE, H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT) is that billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), rejects valid AMI meter reads flagged as high-consumption at import even when received and exported before cutoff: 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (95.5%) show exactly this REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern (E-11), forcing estimate substitution and producing bills customers dispute as wrong.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
